clue.text: Trainee hangs round hospital? That's fishy

indicators.note: something that hangs round another surrounds it, so the trainee's word wraps the hospital letter

parts.note: a cub is a novice or trainee, as in a cub reporter
H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Someone suspects a trainee loitering near a hospital is up to no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's fishy' sounds like suspicion; read literally it says 'that is a fish'.
explanation.definitionFit: The chub is a freshwater fish of the carp family, so it is literally fishy.

clue.text: Kipling's boy has on old garment

parts.note: Kim is the boy hero of Rudyard Kipling's novel Kim

explanation.surface: Kipling's young hero is wearing some antique item of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link word here, joining the boy to ON and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A kimono is a loose robe from Japan, a traditional item of clothing.

clue.text: What domestic arsonist may do? One gives a warning

definitions.meaning: someone setting fire to a home would set a dwelling alight, read as two words
a coastal tower whose beam warns ships away from rocks

explanation.surface: A riddle about a fire-raiser at home, then a description of something that warns.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the answer into a verb and a noun: set fire to (LIGHT) a dwelling (HOUSE).
explanation.definitionFit: A coastal beacon tower flashes its lamp to warn sailors of danger, so it gives a warning.

clue.text: In a row, angry, after inconclusive result

indicators.note: the angry word comes after the result word, so it is placed second

parts.note: a tie is a drawn contest with no winner
to see red or be red in the face is to be angry

explanation.surface: Someone is quarrelling furiously after a match ended in a draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a row' suggests a quarrel, fitting 'angry', but it means arranged in rows or layers.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiered seating is arranged in rows, one level above another.

clue.text: See great new items of furniture

indicators.note: making something new remakes it, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An invitation to look at some fine new pieces of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' looks like an adjective for the furniture but signals rearranging SEE and GREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: An étagère is a set of open display shelves, a piece of household furnishing borrowed from French.

clue.text: Omen of wickedness — there's little good in it

indicators.note: the good letter is placed inside the wickedness word, which 'it' refers back to

parts.note: sin is wickedness or wrongdoing
G is the short form, a 'little' version, of good

explanation.surface: A dark portent of evil, with hardly any good to be found in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' points back to the wickedness, so G goes inside SIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign can be a portent of something to come, just as an omen is.

clue.text: Drink up and hang around for a piece of cake

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means the drink word is written bottom to top

parts.note: to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls
to hover is to linger or hang about in one place

explanation.surface: Finish your drink and loiter, and you can grab a slice of cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses SUP to PUS. 'a piece of cake' means something easy, not a pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean a task or opponent that is very easy to deal with.

clue.text: Treated cruelly in short conversation — upset about it

indicators.note: the upset word goes around the shortened conversation word, which 'it' refers back to

parts.note: bruised feelings are hurt ones, so bruised means upset

indicators.note: short means the conversation word loses its final letter

parts.note: talk is conversation, as in a long talk

explanation.surface: Someone mistreated during a brief chat and left upset by it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reads as an anagram signal but means hurt (bruised); 'short' trims a letter to give TAL, and 'about it' wraps the hurt word round that.
explanation.definitionFit: To brutalise someone is to treat them with savage cruelty.

clue.text: Heartless custom associated with India or another country

indicators.note: without its heart, the custom word loses its central letter

parts.note: a habit is a custom or regular practice
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A cruel tradition linked to India or some other nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' removes the middle B from HABIT, leaving HAIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Haiti is a Caribbean nation, so it is a country other than India.

clue.text: Schemer recruiting criminal about to be found out

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked or bent out of shape, so the letters are reworked
something found out is excluded from the group, so this letter is taken from the pool

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A plotter hires a crook who is about to be exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges RECRUITING after 'to be found out' takes away C (circa, about).
explanation.definitionFit: An intriguer is a person who plots or schemes in secret.

clue.text: Member of family in trouble, right to be locked in

indicators.note: locked in means held inside, so the right letter goes inside the trouble word

parts.note: bother is trouble or fuss

explanation.surface: A relative in trouble, rightly due to be jailed.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother is a male sibling, a relative within the family.

clue.text: Good 'uns getting angry — one's been fired

parts.note: taken as written, a dialect form of ones
hot under the collar means angry

explanation.surface: The good guys are losing their temper, and one of them has been sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fired' suggests a sacking but means discharged from a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunshot is a bullet discharged from a gun, so it has been fired.

clue.text: Animal's extreme idleness

definitions.meaning: a slow-moving tree-dwelling mammal of South America
great laziness, one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: Describing a creature's exceptional laziness.
explanation.definitionFit: The slow tree-dwelling mammal is named for laziness, the deadly sin of extreme idleness.

clue.text: Flames apt to get out of control? Colliery finally introduced ____!

definitions.text: Flames apt to get out of control? Colliery finally introduced ____!

indicators.note: introduced means put inside, so the letter goes into the rearranged letters
letters getting out of control run wild and end up in a new order
finally picks the last letter of the word Colliery

explanation.surface: Fire was a danger underground, so mines brought in a protective lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get out of control' rearranges FLAMES APT; 'introduced' puts Y, the end of Colliery, into it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Davy lamp was designed so that its flame could not ignite firedamp in coal mines.

clue.text: Dread terrible wickedness when reckless person appears

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad way, so the letters of Dread are reworked

parts.note: evil is wickedness

explanation.surface: Fear and terrible wickedness accompany a reckless figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' seems to describe wickedness but rearranges DREAD into DARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A daredevil is someone who takes wild risks with no thought for danger.

clue.text: Not up? But you may be up if you are here!

definitions.text: Not up? But you may be up if you are here!

parts.words: Not up? But you may be up if you are here!
parts.note: the lower floor is the opposite of up, yet you are out of bed (up) once you have gone to that floor in the morning

explanation.surface: A riddle playing with two senses of being up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' means upstairs first, then out of bed: a person on the ground floor is not upstairs but is awake.
explanation.definitionFit: The lower floor of a house is not up, but you must have risen from bed to be there.

clue.text: Wit's formula, so sad, spouted with one passing away?

definitions.text: Wit's formula, so sad, spouted with one passing away?

indicators.note: words spouted come out in a gush, here in a jumbled order
passing away means departing, so this letter is taken from the pool

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A sad quip uttered by someone on their deathbed.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: 'spouted' signals the rearrangement once 'passing away' removes I (one), and the dying speaker is the 'one passing away'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used for a dying person's final remark, often ironically for a rash prediction.

clue.text: Most convivial male monarch, one in repose

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher of the Queen

indicators.note: in places the one letter inside the repose word

parts.note: rest is repose
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cheerful king, the jolliest man around, lying at rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Merriest means most jolly, the most cheerful company at a gathering.

clue.text: Wicked woman posing Spooner's question about existence

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the first sounds of words, so the two words trade their openings

parts.note: a question beginning what is
life is existence, the question being about it

explanation.surface: A sinful woman asking a philosophical question in a muddled way.
explanation.walkthrough: Spooner's swap turns 'What's life?' into the biblical figure; in Genesis she disobeyed and looked back at Sodom.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis she disobeyed God's command not to look back and became a pillar of salt.

clue.text: Chaps in the wrong newspaper boss harassed

indicators.note: in puts the chaps inside the wrong word

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
chaps are men
ED is short for editor, the boss of a newspaper

explanation.surface: Men falsely accused were hounded by a newspaper editor.
explanation.definitionFit: To be tormented is to be harassed or made to suffer repeatedly.

clue.text: Pollute narrow passage

definitions.meaning: a gorge or pass through which troops must march in single file

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to make impure; the noun is a narrow gorge between hills.

clue.text: A broken bit in tall building

definitions.meaning: a sharp fragment of glass or pottery
a skyscraper in London, the tallest in the UK

explanation.surface: A fragment lodged in a skyscraper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Shard is a pointed glass skyscraper by London Bridge, Britain's tallest building.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragment of glass or pottery is the common noun; London's pointed skyscraper borrows the name.

clue.text: Dramatically represent a cold solicitor

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a tout solicits custom, one who solicits rather than a lawyer

explanation.surface: Portraying a chilly lawyer on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' looks like a lawyer but here means a tout, one who solicits trade.
explanation.definitionFit: To act out a scene is to perform or mime it, representing it dramatically.

clue.text: Feeling bad — at rock bottom?

definitions.meaning: ill or poorly, unwell and confined to bed
literally placed in the lowest position, put down at the base

explanation.surface: Feeling miserable and at one's lowest ebb.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means struck down by illness, and read literally means placed in the lowest spot.

clue.text: Rod very briefly disappearing with nasty look

indicators.note: a disappearing letter vanishes, so it is taken out of the rod word

parts.note: a lever is a rigid rod or bar used to shift a load
V is the short form of very

explanation.surface: Rod vanishes briefly, leaving with an unpleasant expression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rod' looks like a man's name but means a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A leer is a sly, lecherous or malicious sidelong glance.

clue.text: Frenzied female in charge full of bluster

indicators.note: the outer letters are filled with the bluster word placed inside them

parts.note: a rant is loud blustering talk

explanation.surface: A woman in authority who is wild and full of bluster.
explanation.definitionFit: Frantic describes someone wild with worry or agitation, a frenzied state.

clue.text: Insincere talk when philosopher is given a hearing

indicators.note: heard out loud, the philosopher's name gives the same sound as another word

parts.note: Immanuel Kant was an 18th-century German philosopher

explanation.surface: A philosopher's empty words are finally listened to.
explanation.definitionFit: Cant is hypocritical, pious-sounding talk that the speaker does not truly mean.

clue.text: Expert finds more faults, sadly — nothing missed

indicators.note: sadly suggests things going wrong, so the letters end up in a new order
something missed is left out, so this letter is dropped from the pool

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A specialist spots more flaws, regretting that nothing escaped notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' signals the rearrangement and 'missed' removes O (nothing) from the pool; 'finds' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A masterful performance shows great skill, as an expert's would.

clue.text: City children (not just one of them) outside old university

indicators.note: the remaining letters sit outside, around the old university letters
not just one of them tells us to remove the singular from the plural word, leaving its ending

parts.note: one child is a single member of the children

explanation.surface: Children from the city, more than one, around an old university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not just one of them' removes the singular from the plural, leaving REN; 'outside' wraps that round O and U.
explanation.definitionFit: Rouen is a historic city in Normandy, France, where Joan of Arc was burned.
